data.title: Suspicious final demand from EuroClaim (Cyprus)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Cyprus) demands €287.40 by 6 August 2026 for an alleged phone-concluded lottery subscription, threatening seizure, a SCHUFA entry and criminal complaint. The letter shows several strong scam indicators.
data.explanation: This looks like a scam or at least a very dubious claim. It uses extreme pressure (72 hours), asks for payment to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private person, and adds unexplained fees. It threatens actions a debt collector cannot simply carry out without a court title, and it says objecting is pointless, which is not true. Do not pay right away. Check whether you ever made such a contract. Ask in writing for proof of the claim and dispute it. Consider contacting a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police. Keep the letter as evidence.

warnings: Extreme pressure: 72-hour deadline and threats of seizure, SCHUFA entry and criminal complaint without further notice.
Payment is demanded to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual (A. Petrauskas) instead of the named company.
The letter is addressed generically to 'Schuldner/in' and gives no contract details, date or proof of the alleged phone contract.
Collection and processing fees appear inflated and unexplained, and the claim that an objection is pointless is false.
A collection agency cannot seize an account without a court title (e.g. Vollstreckungsbescheid).
